# AILANG Parse

> Universal document parser **and generator**. Parses 17 formats into one block schema and writes documents back out in 9 (DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, ODT, ODP, ODS, HTML, Markdown, QMD) — to author a document, write Markdown and convert it. Deterministic Office (DOCX/PPTX/XLSX/ODT/ODP/ODS/HTML/MD/CSV/EPUB/EML/TEX) in milliseconds. PDFs deterministically via `pdftotext` by default (v0.21+), with local Docling / LiteParse backends, or via AI for scans. Comments and PDF annotations are extracted with author attribution and anchored to the text they annotate (v0.23+). Deterministic RAG chunking, no AI (v0.27+). Image files via AI (audio and video are self-host only). One block schema for every format. Available as a hosted MCP server, a local MCP stdio server, and a REST API.

This file follows the [llmstxt.org](https://llmstxt.org) convention. Agents should fetch [llms-full.txt](llms-full.txt) for the complete agent-oriented reference (sign-in, tool catalog, REST examples).

## Essentials

- **Hosted MCP connector (AI clients)**: `https://docparse.ailang.sunholo.com/mcp/connect/` — signs in with **OAuth**: a call without a token gets 401, the client opens the sign-in page, the user signs in with Google or GitHub and approves, and the client keeps the token. No API key in tool arguments.
- **Agent surface (headless agents)**: `https://docparse.ailang.sunholo.com/mcp/` — the same tools, authenticated with a `dp_` key sent as `Authorization: Bearer` or `X-API-Key` (or the `apiKey` argument). An agent without a key gets one with the RFC 8628 device flow: `mcpAuth` → the user approves in a browser → poll `mcpAuthPoll`.
- **Hosted REST API**: `https://docparse.ailang.sunholo.com/api/v1/*` with a `dp_` key in a header.
- **Sending a document**: `content` + `filename` (text, or base64 with `contentEncoding="base64"`), a public `https://` URL, or a sample id. The server never reads a path on the caller's machine.
- **Discovery**: Call `mcpFormats` (no auth) for formats, samples and how to send a document.
- **Generating a document**: write Markdown, then `mcpConvert` (send it as `content` with `filename: "notes.md"`) or `POST /api/v1/convert`, to any of the 9 output formats. Over MCP the result carries `download_url`, a one-hour link to the file; it also comes back inline — branch on `encoding` (`base64` for the ZIP containers, `utf8` for html/md/qmd). Prompt-based AI generation is CLI-only, not on the hosted API.

## Optional

- [docs.html](docs.html): full documentation index
- [document-generation.html](document-generation.html): generating DOCX/PPTX/XLSX/ODT/ODP/ODS/HTML/MD/QMD from Markdown — what survives, what cannot
- [docx-to-markdown.html](docx-to-markdown.html): Microsoft MarkItDown vs AILANG Parse for Word (DOCX) to Markdown; DOCX to clean Markdown for LLMs/RAG with comments, tracked changes (insert/delete/move), nested lists, merged cells and header/footer kept; side-by-side output vs MarkItDown on public files, DOCX benchmark scores, CLI/batch/API commands
- [pdf-to-word.html](pdf-to-word.html): PDF back to an editable Word document styled by your own `--reference-doc`; reading the PDF is the lossy step, what is recovered (headings, lists, tables, running header/footer) and which `--pdf-backend` to choose
- [pdf-to-powerpoint.html](pdf-to-powerpoint.html): a PDF deck back to editable PPTX slides in your own `--reference-doc` template; one slide per page, titles/bullets/tables editable, diagram pages kept as a picture with their text in the speaker notes
- [templates.html](templates.html): free editable Word proposal templates plus matching `--reference-doc` styling references, with the OOXML source and the AILANG builder that assembles them
- [why.html](why.html): why deterministic Office parsing matters
- [benchmarks.html](benchmarks.html): OfficeDocBench results vs Docling, LlamaParse, MarkItDown
- [chunking.html](chunking.html): deterministic RAG chunking — four strategies, blocks never split, per-chunk citation provenance
- [sec-filings.html](sec-filings.html): SEC EDGAR filings — Anthropic's 421-page S-1 parsed into sections, tables and page numbers; read, compare, ask AI, export
- [comments.html](comments.html): comment extraction across DOCX/XLSX/PPTX/PDF, anchored to the annotated span
- [pdf-parsing.html](pdf-parsing.html): PDF backends and annotation (highlight/sticky-note) extraction
- [email-parsing.html](email-parsing.html): EML/MBOX, attachment chain parsing, PDF attachments with automatic OCR

## All pages, by what you want to do

### Convert: Turn one kind of document into another.

- [Word (DOCX) to Markdown](docx-to-markdown.html): Clean Markdown with comments, tracked changes and lists kept. Compared with MarkItDown.
- [PDF to Word](pdf-to-word.html): An editable Word document from a PDF, styled by your own template.
- [PDF to PowerPoint](pdf-to-powerpoint.html): Editable slides from a PDF deck, in your own template.
- [Markdown to Word, PowerPoint and Excel](document-generation.html): Write Markdown once and get DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, ODT or Quarto.
- [Word proposal templates](templates.html): Free editable templates, and how to style generated documents with your own.

### Compare: How AILANG Parse differs from other parsers, with the evidence.

- [Word (DOCX) to Markdown](docx-to-markdown.html): Clean Markdown with comments, tracked changes and lists kept. Compared with MarkItDown.
- [Benchmarks](benchmarks.html): The leading parsers scored on the same Office files, with results you can rerun.
- [Unstructured vs AILANG Parse](migrate-from-unstructured.html): Switch your Office documents by changing one line of code.
- [Direct parsing vs PDF conversion](vs-pdf-conversion.html): What is lost when a Word file is turned into a PDF before parsing.
- [Why AILANG Parse](why.html): Why reading the Office file directly beats parsing a picture of it.

### Extract: The parts of a document other tools lose.

- [Track changes](track-changes.html): Every insertion, deletion and move, with who made it and when.
- [Comments](comments.html): Review comments with author, date, replies and the text they are attached to.
- [Tables and merged cells](tables.html): Every value in its own row and column, merged cells included.
- [Chunking for RAG](chunking.html): Split documents into embedding-sized pieces without cutting a table or losing its heading.
- [SEC filings](sec-filings.html): A 421-page S-1 as sections, tables and page numbers you can search and question.

### Formats: What is read from each file type.

- [Word (DOCX)](docx-parsing.html): Track changes, comments, tables, headers, footers and images.
- [Excel (XLSX)](xlsx-parsing.html): Every sheet, merged cells, formulas and cell types.
- [PowerPoint (PPTX)](pptx-parsing.html): Slides, speaker notes, tables and shapes.
- [PDF](pdf-parsing.html): PDFs with real text are read with no AI and no key. AI for scans, when you ask for it.
- [HTML](html-parsing.html): Tables, headings and lists from web pages and email bodies.
- [Email (EML, MBOX)](email-parsing.html): Headers, body and attachments, with the attachments parsed too.
- [OpenDocument Text (ODT)](odt-parsing.html): LibreOffice Writer files: headings, tables, lists and images.
- [OpenDocument Spreadsheet (ODS)](ods-parsing.html): LibreOffice Calc files: every sheet, with merged cells.
- [OpenDocument Presentation (ODP)](odp-parsing.html): LibreOffice Impress files: slide by slide, with tables and images.
- [EPUB](epub-parsing.html): Ebooks chapter by chapter, with metadata and images.
- [LaTeX and arXiv](latex-parsing.html): Equations, citations and bibliography from the .tex source.
- [Rich Text (RTF)](rtf-parsing.html): Older forms and templates, with no Word or LibreOffice needed.

### Connect: Use it from an AI assistant, your code or your pipeline.

- [ChatGPT, Claude and Codex](connect.html): Add one URL, sign in, and your assistant can read, convert and edit documents.
- [MCP server](mcp.html): The tools an AI agent gets, and how to configure any MCP client.
- [Claude Code plugin](claude-code.html): Install the plugin and parse documents from your terminal.
- [API and SDKs](api.html): REST API with Python, JavaScript, Go and R clients.
- [Integrations](integrations.html): Use it alongside Unstructured, Docling or LlamaParse in an existing pipeline.
- [SuperDoc for legal review](superdoc.html): Read contracts with their redlines, then write changes back.

### Try, run and buy: In the browser, on your machine, or hosted.

- [Workbench](workbench.html): Drop files in your browser and see what comes out. No account.
- [Run locally](selfhost.html): Install the command-line tool and parse on your own machine.
- [Performance guide](performance.html): Parse whole folders quickly.
- [Pricing](pricing.html): Per document, not per page. Free tier included.
